correctness.rationale: At x∈[0,1] the Zak transform is the sum of two convergent geometric series U/(1−r/z)+Vz/(1−sz); the unitary Zak representation for modulation step 1/2 has multiplier |Zg(x,ω)|²+|Zg(x,ω+1/2)|² without extra factor. Writing u=cos(2πω), the rational function F_x(u) has strictly positive second derivative on [−1,1] because its numerator is nonnegative and nondecreasing and its denominator is the product of two positive decreasing affine terms. Therefore F_x(u)+F_x(−u) is strictly increasing with |u|, establishing frequency min at 1/4 and max at 0 modulo 1/2. The maximum spatial fiber is a strictly convex positive combination of e^(−2ax),e^(2bx),e^((b−a)x) with equal endpoint values, hence x=0 on the Zak torus. At ω=1/4, the matrix [[D,−H],[−H,E]] has determinant (1−rs)²/((1+r²)²(1+s²)²)>0; its derivative becomes bE τ²−(b−a)Hτ−aD with exactly one positive root τ=V/U, giving the unique interior minimum x_*. Fresh independent Zak multiplier checks on 5,766 space-frequency samples over six asymmetric/equal decay pairs and 49 exact rational Gram determinant identities all passed. These bounded checks corroborate, but do not replace, the continuous full-parameter proof.
